title: Safety Monitor Firmware Layer
scope: Boot-time reset reason classification (brownout, WDT, panic, power-on, software)
Runtime thermal shutdown: ≥ 373.15 K for 3 consecutive 100 ms samples
Runtime overcurrent shutdown: ≥ 45.0 A for 3 consecutive 100 ms samples
SAFE_HALT flag set before esp_restart() so PC telemetry parser sees event
Lock-free volatile float safety snapshot in sensor_pipeline (never blocks)
New telemetry flag bits: BROWNOUT (12), THERMAL_SHUTDOWN (13), WATCHDOG_RESET (14)
Updated app_main.c: safety_monitor_init() called first at boot
updated_files: main/sensor_pipeline.c     — added volatile float safety snapshot, get_safety_snapshot()

safety_invariants.never_blocks: safety_monitor_task() reads volatile floats — no mutex, no I2C, no blocking
safety_invariants.no_callbacks_under_lock: safety_halt() is called after releasing all locks
safety_invariants.halt_before_restart: SAFE_HALT + event flags written before esp_restart() — 100 ms UART drain
safety_invariants.no_malloc: static state only, zero heap allocation in realtime path
safety_invariants.idempotent_halt: double-halt is a no-op; flags do not change after first halt

test_coverage.A_reset_reason_classification: 5 scenarios: power-on, brownout, watchdog, panic, software
test_coverage.B_string_api: 2 assertions: non-NULL string for each reason
